description: Agent Risk: submit one planned action’s outcomes, what the principal can absorb and how the downside was put to them: the action with its id and description; each outcome with its id, what happens, what it costs the principal, its unit, its likelihood (likely, possible, unlikely or remote, a remote outcome read as not credible), whether the loss can be got back (such as through a chargeback or insurance) and whether the plan names it as the worst credible outcome; the principal’s capacity with the most loss they can absorb, its unit and where that figure comes from; the statement to the principal as written, read for wording that denies the downside such as risk-free or guaranteed, or softens it such as minimal risk; and optionally the share of the capacity at which a loss counts as severe (50 when left out). The signed report gives every outcome with whether it is credible and its share of the capacity, the capacity with the worst credible outcome and its share, the statement with any denying or softening wording and whether it gives the worst loss as a figure, and counts the outcomes credible, remote, recoverable and over the capacity, and names an unacceptable downside: a worst credible loss over what the principal can absorb, a statement that denies the downside while a credible loss exists and a named worst outcome smaller than the largest credible loss; then a worst loss at a large share of the capacity, a worst loss that cannot be got back, softening wording, a statement without the worst loss as a figure and no outcome named as the worst, with the fix for each. Outcomes compare only in the capacity’s unit. This reads the worst credible outcome of one action against what the principal can absorb: the value handed over before a counterparty pays in one proposed agreement is wever_negotiation-risk-check, who pays when an agent errs under pre-purchase terms is wever_liability-terms-check and the range around an estimate is wever_uncertainty-range-check. Verdict risk_downside_unacceptable, risk_downside_severe, risk_downside_unstated or risk_downside_acceptable. POST /api/risk-downside-check. Reads only the recorded material about the planned action in the call: no network request, fetch, money movement, message, configuration change or external write; the planned action is not taken, paused, approved or undone and no limit, position or dependency is changed. Agent Risk reads the consequences of an action the agent plans to take, before it takes it: how much it puts at stake against the agent’s limits, whether it can be undone, how far a failure would spread beyond its target, the worst credible outcome against what the principal can absorb, whether it piles value into one place, what it depends on staying available or true, whether acting now is itself the risk and whether repeating or chaining it multiplies the risk. It is not confidence in information (the wever_uncertainty checks read how sure the information behind a decision is; a risk check reads what the action costs if it goes wrong: uncertainty is about what the agent knows, risk is about what the action can do), not permission (wever_consent-scope-check reads whether the principal’s grant covers a use and wever_authority-scope-check reads whether the agent may act at all; a risk check reads the consequences of an action already permitted, and a permission never makes an action safe), not an agreement’s exposure (wever_negotiation-risk-check reads the value handed over before a counterparty pays under one proposed agreement; a risk check reads one action the agent is about to take) and not sorting work (the wever_triage checks sort, route and escalate a queue of work; a risk check assesses one planned action before it runs). Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-risk-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-risk/.

absorbable.description: The most loss the principal can absorb.

basis.description: Where that figure comes from, such as the principal’s stated loss limit.

unit.description: The unit amounts are counted in, such as USDC.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

outcomes.description: The outcomes the action can lead to if it goes wrong.

id.description: The outcome id, such as o1.

likelihood.description: Likely, possible, unlikely or remote; a remote outcome is not credible.

outcome.description: What happens, such as the goods never arrive.

recoverable.description: The principal can get the loss back, such as through a chargeback or insurance.

unit.description: The unit amounts are counted in, such as USDC.

worst.description: The plan names this as its worst credible outcome.

text.description: The downside as put to the principal, read for wording that denies it, such as risk-free, or softens it, such as minimal risk.

warn_percent.description: A worst loss at or above this share of what the principal can absorb counts as severe; 50 when left out.

name: wever_risk-downside-check
title: Risk downside check
